history.summary: NOT A HINDU TEMPLE - keep-or-drop decision needed. This is a Muslim congregational mosque (jama masjid) in Salem city, Tamil Nadu. It is Salem's oldest mosque, standing on the southern bank of the Thirumanimutharu river in the heart of the city (V Market Road, 1st Agraharam). It was reportedly built by the Mysore ruler Tipu Sultan, who is said to have offered prayers here; the masjid inam granted to the mosque in 1862 was confirmed by the British with a special resolution in 1880. IDENTITY FLAG: 'Jama Masjid' is a generic title and Salem has several mosques; this entry documents the best-supported one - the Jamia/Jamiya Masjid at V Market Road, 1st Agraharam, Salem Fort (geocode 11.65468, 78.15958; phone 0427-2267227 per the Tamil Nadu government portal). The media image is from a Salem tourism page and its exact identity as this mosque is not confirmed (verify). OPENING-HOURS CONFLICT: the state government portal lists 9:30 AM-6:00 PM while a travel article lists 6:00 AM-8:00 PM (unresolved). One travel article also carries a garbled editorial claim that this mosque 'is home to one of the 108 Shiva Lingas of Salem' - plainly erroneous; do not use that claim.
